Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe exactly how your right leg is positioned and where precisely the groin pain is located? Also, were you wearing a seatbelt during the rear-end collision, and did you experience any immediate numbness or loss of sensation in your leg?
Klaus Mueller

Yes, I was wearing my seatbelt, and right after the crash, my right leg just felt stuck in a twisted position where it looks shorter and is turned inward. The pain is deep in my right groin and shoots down my thigh, but I can still feel my leg and toes, so there's no numbness. It's just so painful that I can't move it back to a normal position.
Maria Lopez
My right leg is turned outward and slightly shortened, and the pain is deep in the crease of my groin. I wasn't wearing a seatbelt, and I felt immediate numbness on the outside of my right foot.
Klaus Mueller

That's not quite right; my leg is actually turned inward, not outward, and I was definitely wearing my seatbelt. I don't have any numbness in my foot, just severe pain deep in my groin where my leg feels stuck in that twisted position.
Maria Lopez

Do you have any numbness in your perineal area or difficulty controlling your bladder, and is the pain severe enough to prevent you from moving your leg at all? Additionally, have you noticed any swelling or bruising on the thigh or knee since the accident?
Klaus Mueller

No, I don't have any numbness in my perineal area or trouble with my bladder, but the pain is so sharp that I absolutely cannot move my leg from this twisted position. I haven't noticed any significant swelling or bruising on my thigh yet, though my knees are quite sore and painful.
Maria Lopez

No numbness in the perineal area or bladder issues, but the pain is excruciating and I cannot move my leg at all. I do see some swelling on the thigh, but no bruising yet.

Do you have any history of hip problems, osteoporosis, or previous fractures? Also, did you feel a "pop" or "snap" at the moment of impact, and is your knee locked in a specific position? Right_Hip_X-Ray.

Thank you for that information; I am awaiting the results of the hip X-ray to confirm if the femoral head has dislocated from the socket. While we wait, can you tell me if you have any known allergies to anesthesia or pain medication, as you will likely need immediate sedation for reduction? Please also confirm if you felt any specific "click" or if your leg just suddenly gave way during the impact.
